guinness.name: Guinness Storehouse
guinness.price_text: ≈ €26–32 adult online; cheaper booked ahead, under-18s reduced
guinness.hours: Daily, roughly 09:30–19:00 (last entry earlier); check on the day
guinness.tip: Book a timed ticket online and go early to beat the crowds. The Gravity Bar pint is included.
guinness.best: Morning or late afternoon; rainy days

trinity-library.name: Trinity College Library (Book of Kells)
trinity-library.price_text: ≈ €18–25 adult timed ticket; check current price
trinity-library.hours: Daily, roughly 09:30–17:00; times vary by season
trinity-library.tip: Book a timed slot online. The Long Room is the highlight; allow extra time for the exhibition.

temple-bar.name: Temple Bar
temple-bar.price_text: Free to walk; drinks €6–8 a pint
temple-bar.hours: Always open; pubs busiest from evening
temple-bar.tip: It is touristy and pricey. Have one drink for the atmosphere, then eat and drink elsewhere.
temple-bar.best: Evening for live music; daytime for photos

dublin-castle.name: Dublin Castle
dublin-castle.hours: Daily, roughly 09:45–17:15; last entry about an hour before
dublin-castle.tip: The courtyard and gardens are free. Pay only if you want the guided State Apartments tour.

st-patricks.name: St Patrick's Cathedral
st-patricks.price_text: ≈ €8–10 adult; discounts for students and seniors
st-patricks.hours: Mon–Sat roughly 09:00–17:00 · Sun limited visiting hours
st-patricks.tip: Check Sunday times before you go, as services limit visiting. The park next door is a good rest stop.

kilmainham.name: Kilmainham Gaol
kilmainham.tip: Tickets are timed and sell out days ahead. Book online as soon as you know your dates.
kilmainham.best: Book the first tour of the day

christ-church.name: Christ Church Cathedral
christ-church.hours: Daily, roughly 09:30–17:00; check on the day
christ-church.tip: The medieval crypt is the best part. Combine with Dublin Castle, a two-minute walk away.

dublin-zoo.name: Dublin Zoo
dublin-zoo.tip: It is inside Phoenix Park, so plan a walk in the park afterwards. Book online for a small saving.

emerald-park.name: Emerald Park
emerald-park.hours: Seasonal; usually daily in summer, weekends off-season
emerald-park.tip: It is outside the city near Ashbourne. Check transport and opening days before you commit.

fort-lucan.name: Fort Lucan
fort-lucan.tip: An outdoor adventure park aimed at younger children. Confirm it is open before travelling out.

funderland.name: Funderland (travelling theme park)
funderland.price_text: Pay-per-ride or wristband; check on the day
funderland.hours: Temporary pop-up; dates and venue change each year
funderland.tip: It is a seasonal travelling fair, not a fixed site. Check the current dates and location before planning.
funderland.best: Check season; usually winter and summer runs

gpo.name: General Post Office (GPO)
gpo.price_text: Free to view exterior; Witness History centre charged
gpo.hours: Lobby during post office hours; exterior always visible
gpo.tip: Look at the bullet marks on the columns from 1916. The small museum inside tells the Easter Rising story.

grafton.name: Grafton Street
grafton.tip: Busking is part of the scene. Walk it between Trinity and St Stephen's Green.

irish-stew.name: Irish stew (a classic pub dish)
irish-stew.price_text: ≈ €14–20 in a pub; varies by venue
irish-stew.hours: Served at lunch and dinner in most pubs
irish-stew.tip: It is a hearty lamb and potato dish. Try it at a traditional pub away from the main Temple Bar strip for better value.

liffey-cruise.name: Liffey River Cruise
liffey-cruise.tip: A short, easy way to see the city from the water. Book ahead in summer and dress for wind.

molly-malone.name: Molly Malone Statue
molly-malone.tip: A quick photo stop near Trinity. Combine it with Grafton Street and St Stephen's Green.

national-museum.name: National Museum of Ireland – Archaeology
national-museum.hours: Tue–Sat roughly 10:00–17:00 · Sun from 14:00 · closed Monday
national-museum.tip: Free and excellent. See the bog bodies and the Ardagh Chalice; allow at least an hour.

oconnell.name: O'Connell Street
oconnell.tip: Wide boulevard with the Spire and statues. Walk it toward the GPO and the river.

patrick-festival.name: Saint Patrick's Festival
patrick-festival.hours: Around 17 March each year; parade usually midday
patrick-festival.tip: Book accommodation months ahead and arrive early for a parade spot. Expect big crowds and road closures.

trinity-college.name: Trinity College Dublin (campus)
trinity-college.price_text: Free to walk the main square; Book of Kells charged separately
trinity-college.hours: Campus generally open daytime; check on the day
trinity-college.tip: The cobbled front square and the campanile are free to see. The library needs a separate ticket.

vikings.name: Dublin's Viking history (walking tour)
vikings.tip: Dublin was founded as a Viking settlement. A guided walk around Wood Quay and the cathedral area brings it to life.

george-st-arcade.name: George's Street Arcade (food and market hall)
george-st-arcade.price_text: Free to browse; food from about €5
george-st-arcade.tip: A Victorian covered market for a quick lunch or coffee. Good for a rainy break.

stephens-green.name: St Stephen's Green
stephens-green.tip: A calm green escape at the top of Grafton Street. Sit by the lake and feed the ducks.

phoenix-park.name: Phoenix Park and the Papal Cross viewpoint
phoenix-park.hours: Always open; gates for cars close at night
phoenix-park.tip: Huge city park with deer. Rent a bike or walk to the Papal Cross for open views.

howth-cliff.name: Howth cliff walk
howth-cliff.tip: Take the DART to Howth for coastal views and seafood. Wear proper shoes and check the forecast.

literary-pub-tour.name: Traditional music pub session
literary-pub-tour.tip: Ask locally for a pub with a real session, not a staged show. Arrive early for a seat.

coffee-neighbourhood.name: Georgian Dublin door and square walk
coffee-neighbourhood.tip: Walk Merrion and Fitzwilliam Squares to see the famous painted doors and Georgian terraces.
